description: End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock is a public dataset of calibrated and validated 15-minute load profiles for all major residential and commercial building types and end uses, across all climate regions of the United States, offered both as aggregates and as individual modelled building timeseries. It was produced by a three-year project funded by the U.S. Department of Energy, led by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and others, to help cities, states and utilities value energy efficiency, demand response and distributed energy resources; the profiles come from ResStock and ComStock calibrated against many measured datasets, as the methodology report describes. Data date from 14 October 2021 and were last updated on 28 March 2024; the submission's DOI is 10.25984/1876417. Access is through the Open Energy Data Initiative, which hosts the files in its public data lake. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, free. Caveats: profiles describe a synthetic but representative stock, not metered individual customers, and newer ResStock and ComStock releases supersede parts of it. Simulation uses are building-load inputs for capacity planning, distribution network flow studies and demand-flexibility optimisation. Related records: ResStock and ComStock (the models behind it), EnergyPlus.
name: End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock
notes: Formats and releases read from the public OEDI S3 listing (s3://oedi-data-lake/nrel-pds-building-stock/end-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock/2021/): four releases (resstock_amy2018_release_1, resstock_tmy3_release_1, comstock_amy2018_release_1, comstock_tmy3_release_1), each with metadata.parquet, timeseries aggregates as CSV by ASHRAE/IECC climate zone and other geographies, individual building timeseries, building energy models, weather and occupancy schedules.
provider: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (now NLR) with LBNL and partners, for the U.S. Department of Energy; hosted on the Open Energy Data Initiative (OEDI)
